messages:
sara_support: Customer (Acme) reporting SSE stream truncation + partial events when request flows through their gRPC->HTTP1 gateway. Happens on intermittent reconnects, client sees half events and then a new connection resumes duplicate tokens (billing spike). Repro steps below.

sara_support: Repro (simplified):
```
# client opens SSE over http2 to edge -> our gw -> customer gRPC transcoder -> backend (http1)
curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  --http2-prior-knowledge https://edge.redwood.example/v1/stream?mode=sse
```
Headers we observed: `content-type: text/event-stream`, `transfer-encoding: chunked`, `via: grpc-transcode/1.2`

alex_infra: do we know which intermediary is doing chunk boundary splitting? any proxies in their path?

sara_support: customer uses envoy-based gRPC gateway that does http2->http1 transcoding. They sent tcp pcap + app logs. Saw repeating pattern: stream yields short fragments (~512 bytes), connection closes, client reconnects, then receives continuation but without proper event boundary (client treats it as new event fragment).

mike_runtime: possible causes: 1) gateway re-chunking splits SSE event-line boundaries mid-line; 2) our edge or runtime is coalescing/trimming trailers incorrectly on h2->h1 translation; 3) client reconnection semantics (Last-Event-ID) not propagated due to missing SSE-id header.

jenna_engineer: can you paste a short excerpt of the raw fragments from pcap (hex or ascii)? even a few lines showing line breaks would help.

sara_support: pasted snippet from pcap (sanitized):
```
:event: msg
data: partial-body-pa

--connection reset--
# reconnect -> new socket
data: rtial-body-part2

```

sara_support: you can see the event delimiter (blank line) was lost between fragments; client concatenates and ends up with `partial-body-partial-body-part2` but sometimes a spurious newline yields an empty event which the client treats as keepalive and doesn't increment id, causing dedupe issues on reconnect -> duplicate token accounting.

katie_ops: is billing double-count because each reconnect causes our tokenizer to reprocess overlapping bytes? or duplicate tokens are created on resumed requests? need quick impact numbers.

sara_support: customer: ~30% of stream reconnects over last 6 hours, billing shows ~1.8x token usage vs expected for that session. Latency complaints too: extra 200-500ms on reconnect.

mike_runtime: we have a known edge case: when an upstream closes mid-chunk and the runtime switches to fallback path (h2->h1 compatibility mode) we don't always flush the partial line buffer before handing socket up; that can leave a dangling suffix that gets re-emitted on the next connection. I'll add a trace flag to capture the buffer state.

alex_infra: can we get the customer's gateway config? particularly `preserve_streaming` or `buffered_streaming` flags. If their envoys are buffering with `max_request_bytes` small it could force multi-chunk writes.

sara_support: customer sent config snippet: `grpc_transcoder { preserve_streaming: false }` and `http1_buffer: 1024` (defaults). They said they enabled transcoding to support mobile clients.

jenna_engineer: temporary mitigation options: 1) advise customer to enable `preserve_streaming: true` or bump buffer to avoid mid-event splits; 2) on our side we can tweak runtime to flush partial event-lines immediately on upstream close (cheap fix) and add an SSE-aware reassembly step in the gateway (needs careful tests).

mike_runtime: agree. Quick dev step: enable DEBUG trace for stream reassembly at edge (flag: runtime.stream.reassembly=debug). That will show every partial-line buffer and whether we flush on close. I'll instrument and push to a canary.

deploy_bot: deploy queued: runtime-edge-canary-2026-03-17T14:12Z (includes stream.reassembly debug).

katie_ops: assign to eng-runtime + infra to coordinate with customer. Also need to add billing investigation tag: `billing:possible-dup-tokens` to ticket. Customer expects ETA < 24h.

sara_support: noted. I'll send workaround steps to customer (preserve_streaming, bump buffer) and let them know we have a canary. Will capture pcap + token logs to correlate.

alex_infra: one more ask: can the customer include `Last-Event-ID` support on reconnects? if their gateway strips SSE id headers during transcoding that's contributing to dedupe failure.

sara_support: they confirmed `Last-Event-ID` is not currently preserved. adding that to escalation list.

mike_runtime: next actions: 1) roll canary with immediate trace and monitor for reassembly traces; 2) implement flush-on-close fix if traces confirm dangling buffers; 3) add a telemetry counter for `sse.partial_flush_retries` and `sse.duplicate_token_emitted` for billing correlation.

jenna_engineer: will schedule follow-up post-mortem after fix. tagging oncall for notification.

sara_support: thanks team — pinging @alex_infra @mike_runtime once canary is live I'll ask customer to retry. :thumbsup:
